verses.text: Jesus began teaching beside the lake again. A very large crowd gathered around him, so he got into a boat and sat out on the water, while everyone stayed on shore.
He taught them many things through stories. In his teaching he said,
“Listen! A farmer went out to plant seeds.
As he scattered them, some fell along the path, and birds came and ate them up.
Some fell on rocky ground where there wasn’t much soil. They sprouted quickly because the soil wasn’t deep.
But when the sun came up, the plants were scorched. They dried up because they had no roots.
Other seed fell among thornbushes. The thorns grew up and choked it, so it produced no crop.
But some seed fell on good soil. It grew, increased, and produced a crop—some thirty times what was planted, some sixty, and some a hundred.”
Then he said, “Anyone who has ears to hear should listen.”
When Jesus was alone, the people around him, along with the Twelve, asked him about the stories.
He said, “You’ve been given the secret of God’s kingdom. But to those outside, everything is told in stories,
so that ‘they may look and look but not see; they may hear and hear but not understand. Otherwise they might turn back and be forgiven.’”
Then Jesus asked them, “Don’t you understand this story? How will you understand any of the stories?
The farmer plants God’s message.
The seed along the path represents those who hear the message. As soon as they hear it, Satan comes and takes away the message planted in them.
The seed on rocky ground represents those who hear the message and immediately welcome it with joy.
But they have no root and last only a short time. When trouble or persecution comes because of the message, they quickly fall away.
Other seed fell among thornbushes. This represents those who hear the message,
but the worries of this life, the lure of wealth, and desires for other things crowd in and choke the message, so it produces nothing.
The seed in good soil represents those who hear the message, welcome it, and produce a crop—thirty, sixty, or a hundred times what was planted.”
He also said, “Do you bring in a lamp to put it under a basket or a bed? Don’t you put it on a stand?
Whatever is hidden will be brought into the open, and whatever is kept secret will be revealed.
Anyone who has ears to hear should listen.”
He said to them, “Pay attention to what you hear. The measure you use will be measured to you—and even more.
Whoever has will be given more; whoever doesn’t have, even what they have will be taken away.”
He also said, “God’s kingdom is like someone scattering seed on the ground.
Night and day, whether the farmer sleeps or gets up, the seed sprouts and grows, though the farmer doesn’t know how.
The earth produces a crop on its own: first the stalk, then the head, then the full grain in the head.
As soon as the grain is ripe, the farmer puts in the sickle, because harvest time has come.”
He said, “What can we compare God’s kingdom to? What story can we use to explain it?
It’s like a mustard seed, the smallest seed planted in the ground.
But once it’s planted, it grows and becomes the largest garden plant, with branches big enough for the birds to nest in its shade.”
Jesus used many stories like this to share the message with them, as much as they could understand.
He didn’t speak to them without using stories. But when he was alone with his disciples, he explained everything.
That day, when evening came, Jesus said to them, “Let’s cross to the other side.”
They left the crowd and took him with them in the boat, just as he was. Other boats went along too.
A fierce windstorm came up, and waves crashed into the boat until it was filling with water.
Jesus was in the back of the boat, sleeping on a cushion. They woke him and said, “Teacher, don’t you care that we’re going to drown?”
He got up, rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, “Quiet! Be still!” The wind stopped, and everything became calm.
He said to them, “Why are you so afraid? Do you still have no faith?”
They were terrified and said to one another, “Who is this? Even the wind and the sea obey him!”
